All collected trials · no pairs excluded

What happened across three pairs.

Assistance was associated with lower modeled hazard exposure and lower total spending. It also produced fewer completed journeys overall. The comparison retains both benefits and costs.

Mean outcome per round

Three rounds per condition. Cost and pumping efficiency ratios use pooled totals. No overall “AI quality” or optimal-decision percentage is invented.

Every matched pair

How to read efficiency
  • Lower spending is shown alongside cost per completed journey. Doing less is not automatically more efficient.
  • Pump efficiency divides removed water volume by estimated pump mobilization/relocation charges. The costs are model assumptions.
  • Budget compliance was achieved in all six rounds. The $5M fund was not a binding constraint, so unused budget does not establish an assistance advantage.
  • Blocked actions are attempted commands that did not execute. They are not a complete measure of strategic decision quality.
  • Warning occupancy and hazard exposure use different thresholds. Both are shown, including outcomes that favor the human-alone condition.
Study design, limits and provenance
  • One participant completed three matched pairs: A human first, B assistance first, C human first. Order was not fully balanced.
  • All runs use the same physical model version, baseline parameter set, fixed one-hour horizon and 20× experiment speed. Replays can run faster without changing recorded outcomes.
  • Practice, fatigue, repeated scenarios and differences among scenarios may influence results. This dataset does not isolate a general causal AI effect.
  • Station dimensions, task durations, hydraulic connectivity, safety thresholds and mobilization costs are documented educational assumptions, not validated MTA operating specifications.
  • MetroMind is rule-based decision support. The human made decisions in both conditions.
  • Replays show recorded choices and failures, not newly generated advice. Successful actions reconstruct the physical world; exported outcomes remain the source of the comparison.
  • Completed-journey timing excludes unfinished journeys, so completion share and abandonment should be considered alongside it.
